propositions: The plan-review gate's LLM judge exhibits drift in per-finding decisions across repeated runs, injecting noise into the Pass-2 sub-answer vocabulary that downstream stories (R3, R5) depend on.

Section-order permutation of input plans can flip gate verdicts, violating the assumption that the gate's absolute rubric scoring is order-invariant, and must be measured to bound residual order-sensitivity before new order-exposed criteria (like R3's container criterion) land.

Self-consistency testing over 50 findings from the G6/E4/T3 cohort (N≥50, sampled deterministically with frozen committed plan text) must yield Fleiss κ≥0.6 and raw agreement≥0.8 to gate R5's new asserted_capability_confirmed sub-answer.

Order-shuffle stability testing over 14 plans with ≥3 top-level sections (3 distinct deterministic permutations per plan: identity + 2 seeded shuffles) must yield Fleiss κ≥0.6 and raw agreement≥0.8 on verdict to gate R3's container criterion.

Infrastructure-level INDETERMINATE verdicts (those carrying coverage.llm_unavailable or coverage.verify_failed flags) are execution failures, not stable judge outcomes, and must be dropped and re-run until 3 substantive verdicts are collected per finding/permutation.

E6 measures stochastic stability of the existing gate's Pass-2/Pass-3 judge through re-execution and inter-rater agreement (κ, raw agreement), not through circular accuracy-adjudication against gate-generated labels.
